methodology.javascript: Repeated pairs: full npm ci/typecheck/lint/bundle with receipt creation, followed by verified reuse of the exact validated inputs and six outputs. npm transfer time is included; the dependency download cache is not reset.
methodology.compression: Repeated pairs: exact uncached report, separately recorded cache population, then reuse of that populated cache. Same file bytes, gzip9, Brotli11 and Node implementation; report stdout must be byte-identical.
methodology.limits: These measure avoided repeated build-tool work, not Rust compilation, cold full builds, runtime rendering, or whole CI. Speedup is median baseline seconds divided by median reuse seconds.

follow_up.diagnosis: Placeholder geometry substitution writes OUT_DIR/placeholder/App.xaml; the asset loop then emits rerun-if-changed for that generated work file, allowing it to invalidate its own first repeat.
follow_up.separate_fix: Retain original document and geometry input watches; embed transformed UTF-8 text directly in the generated Rust asset table; keep intermediate as build-script work data rather than a rustc include_bytes input.
follow_up.validation_required: Independent population/first-repeat pairs, semantic asset bytes, source/geometry invalidation, and compilation after intermediate deletion, tied to the subsequent source revision and CI run.
follow_up.comparison_scope: A subsequent main-baseline CI experiment includes both the earlier SampleBuild optional-file fix and the ControlCatalog placeholder-input fix. An ea26d568 baseline isolates the latter; neither comparison was measured in the runs recorded here.

limits: Cache replay uses an empty target and a populated local compiler cache; remote restore/upload and tool installation are excluded.
Scanner, unchanged sample, local compiler-cache, browser tooling and cold theme graph are different workloads; ratios cannot be combined into a whole-workspace or whole-CI speedup.
All comparisons are paired within the new run; differences from earlier run timings are not controlled cross-run performance comparisons.
All ratios use their own matched experiments; absolute times from different jobs/runners/revisions must not be treated as a matched level-2 versus level-3 comparison.
The nine benchmark reports include two separate browser workloads. Full per-unit raw lists remain in the digest-verified linked artifacts rather than being duplicated for every sample here.
Platform job success respects existing continue-on-error policy; the optional Windows automation failures are reported explicitly and match all 224 main-baseline case outcomes.
Existing ignored tests and hardware/software rendering fallbacks remain; job-level test counts overlap and are not a count of unique workspace tests.
Windows catalog build durations are observations before the separately implemented placeholder-input fix, not a controlled catalog speedup measurement.
